sheets.prompt:
Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character, outfit and proportions in every panel; plain background. The first reference image is only the panel layout guide: copy its four-panel arrangement, not its grey mannequin shapes. Layout detail: the sheet looks like four photographs mounted side by side on one horizontal board, divided from left to right by three vertical gaps into four equal tall narrow panels, each a separate small photo of the same animal; never paint it as one single continuous picture. Panel 1 (left): full-body front view, the guinea-pig facing the camera. Panel 2: full-body side profile. Panel 3: full-body view from behind. Panel 4 (tall right column): close-up of the head and shoulders, facing the camera. In each full-body panel the animal is scaled down in perspective to fit completely inside the tall narrow panel, sitting on a small patch of plain floor with a soft contact shadow and plenty of empty backdrop above it. Plain soft grey-green studio backdrop in every panel, even soft daylight, no scenery, no captions or labels.

Subject: one juror of the Wonderland trial, a male guinea-pig (Cavia porcellus), a photoreal CGI animal about 25 cm long, a mature adult: very round, short-haired, ginger-tan and white piebald coat, small dark eyes, pink ears, pink nose and fine whiskers; naturalistic guinea-pig anatomy with short legs and tiny feet, no cartoon face. Faint grey slate-pencil dust on his front paws. Costume rule for the whole jury, quoted verbatim: 'unclothed and unadorned: eleven bare natural animals and birds as jurors, wearing nothing' - so this single guinea-pig, the only animal on the sheet, wears nothing at all: no clothes, no collar, no accessories. Beside him on the floor in panel 1 lies his small framed school slate and a slate pencil, sized to him.

Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.

Layout recap (highest priority): four separate tall panels side by side, exactly one guinea-pig in each panel, the same individual in front / side / back full-body views and one head close-up; no other animals.
